builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Attention, Dynamic Wave and Hybrid Sequence Mixers in Language Models
summary: The method replaces multi-head attention with an input-dependent damped-oscillation recurrence, or mixes both in a hybrid stack. The quality gain of the hybrid comes at the cost of inheriting its more expensive mixer (peak VRAM matching the pure Transformer to 0.1%), and the claimed memory and latency advantages disappear entirely once attention uses a standard fused SDPA kernel and the recurrence loop is optimized. Adoption can fail because the results are demonstrated only at 10.94M parameters on TinyStories, so neither the perplexity gain nor the efficiency profile is validated at production model scale or on realistic workloads.
rationale: The paper itself shows the efficiency case collapses against the fused attention kernels the reader already gets from standard frameworks, leaving only a small-scale quality signal that does not justify replacing a mature attention stack under constrained infrastructure.
technique: Dynamic Wave recurrent mixer and hybrid attention

claims.statement: The method replaces multi-head attention with an input-dependent damped-oscillation recurrence, or mixes both in a hybrid stack. The quality gain of the hybrid comes at the cost of inheriting its more expensive mixer (peak VRAM matching the pure Transformer to 0.1%), and the claimed memory and latency advantages disappear entirely once attention uses a standard fused SDPA kernel and the recurrence loop is optimized. Adoption can fail because the results are demonstrated only at 10.94M parameters on TinyStories, so neither the perplexity gain nor the efficiency profile is validated at production model scale or on realistic workloads.

Hybrid Wave-Attention reaches 5.95 perplexity on TinyStories versus 6.93 for a pure Transformer at 10.94M parameters; memory savings of 78.7% at 4096 tokens exist only against an unfused attention baseline and vanish against fused SDPA (1404.3 MB vs 1403.6 MB).
